title: Division 855 — capital gains and foreign residents
summary: Foreign residents disregard capital gains and losses unless the CGT asset is taxable Australian property (TAP) — direct or indirect interests in Australian real property, or assets used through an Australian permanent establishment. The TAP classification (s 855-15 table) is the boundary: real property (855-20), indirect interests (855-25 with the non-portfolio and principal asset tests), PE assets (855-35 reduction), options/rights, and fixed-trust interests (855-40). Subdiv 855-B handles becoming an Australian resident: market value cost base reset (855-45, subject to TAP and pre-1985 exceptions), trust becoming resident (855-50) and CFCs (855-55 via ITAA 1936 ss 411-414). Subsection coverage: operative 855-10(1)-(2), 855-15, 855-20, 855-25(1)-(2), 855-30, 855-32, 855-35(1)-(3), 855-40(1)-(3), 855-45(1)-(3), 855-50(1)-(2), 855-55(1)-(4) mapped to nodes; 855-5 (objects), 855-16 (definition), 855-1 (guide) contextual.

nodes.label: Is a foreign resident (or trustee of a foreign trust for CGT purposes) a party to a CGT event just before it happens?
nodes.body: Division 855 lets foreign residents disregard capital gains and losses unless the underlying CGT asset is taxable Australian property (TAP) — a direct or indirect interest in Australian real property, a PE business asset, or an option/right to acquire such assets. The foreign-resident/foreign-trustee status is tested just before the CGT event (s 855-10(1)(a)). Separate rules apply when an individual/company becomes an Australian resident (Subdiv 855-B).

nodes.label: Is the CGT asset taxable Australian property (TAP)?
nodes.body: TAP has 5 categories (s 855-15 table): (1) taxable Australian real property (s 855-20); (2) an indirect Australian real property interest (s 855-25) not covered by item 5; (3) a CGT asset used at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian PE (DTA meaning where applicable, s 855-16); (4) an option or right to acquire an asset covered by item 1, 2 or 3; (5) a CGT asset covered by s 104-165(3) (choosing to disregard gain/loss on ceasing to be an Australian resident). Special rule (s 855-10(2)): for CGT events D1, D2, F1 and J1, the relevant asset is the UNDERLYING asset (e.g. the land subject to an easement, option or lease).

nodes.label: Gain or loss is disregarded (s 855-10)
nodes.body: If the CGT asset is not TAP (none of items 1-5 of s 855-15, having regard to the s 855-10(2) underlying-asset rule for D1/D2/F1/J1 events), the capital gain or loss from the CGT event is disregarded — the foreign resident has no Australian CGT exposure on that asset. This is the core Div 855 relief.

nodes.label: Is the asset taxable Australian real property (real property in Australia, or mining/quarrying/prospecting rights)?
nodes.body: Taxable Australian real property is real property situated in Australia (including a lease of land) or a mining, quarrying or prospecting right (to the extent not real property) where the minerals, petroleum or quarry materials are in Australia (s 855-20).

nodes.label: Is the asset an indirect Australian real property interest (membership interests in an entity)?
nodes.body: A membership interest is an indirect Australian real property interest if it passes both the non-portfolio interest test (s 960-195: 10%+ of the entity's membership interests) and the principal asset test (s 855-30: the market value of the entity's taxable Australian real property exceeds the market value of all its other assets) — ss 855-25(1)(a)-(b). The 12-month lookback applies (interest must pass the tests now, or throughout a 12-month period ending within the last 24 months).

nodes.label: Did you use the asset at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian permanent establishment?
nodes.body: An asset used at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian PE is TAP (s 855-15 item 3), using the DTA permanent establishment article meaning where the taxpayer is resident in a treaty country (s 855-16). s 855-35 reduces the gain/loss where the asset was used for the PE business for only part of the holding period. If the asset was NOT used through a PE, check the remaining TAP categories (items 4 and 5) before concluding.

nodes.label: Gain is assessable / loss can be claimed — normal CGT rules apply
nodes.body: TAP assets of foreign residents remain in the Australian CGT net. The gain is included in assessable income (Div 102) and the loss is available under the normal rules. For indirect interests, the entity-level principal asset test and non-portfolio threshold apply (s 855-25/855-30).

nodes.label: FACET — Main residence exemption is limited for foreign residents (Div 118-B)
nodes.body: A foreign resident cannot claim the main residence exemption for CGT events after 30 June 2020 (s 118-110(4)-(5)) unless they made the lifetime choice under s 118-145. This is NOT a TAP classification category — it is a separate exemption question under Div 118-B, distinct from the s 855-15 TAP table and s 855-35 (PE business asset reduction).

nodes.label: FACET — Fixed trust interests (s 855-40)
nodes.body: s 855-40 provides comparable treatment for indirect ownership through a fixed trust: a gain in respect of your interest in a fixed trust is disregarded if the asset would not have been TAP had you held it directly. This supplements the direct TAP classification, not replaces it.

nodes.label: You become an Australian resident (Subdiv 855-B)
nodes.body: When an individual or company becomes an Australian resident, CGT assets owned just before that time get a market value cost base reset (s 855-45), subject to exceptions. This is a separate trigger from the Subdiv 855-A foreign-resident disposal rules.

statute.title: Individual or company becomes an Australian resident

rulings.title: 855-45(3) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

nodes.label: Is the asset taxable Australian property, acquired before 20 Sep 1985, or an excluded ESS interest?
nodes.body: The s 855-45 cost base reset does not apply to: (a) assets that are TAP (they keep their existing cost base); (b) pre-CGT assets acquired before 20 September 1985; (c) ESS interests covered by Subdiv 83A-C with a deferred taxing point that has not yet occurred, and start-up ESS interests within s 83A-33(1)(a)-(c) (s 855-45(4)). The whole section is subject to s 768-950: temporary residents immediately after becoming Australian residents do not get the reset (s 855-45(1) note).

rulings.title: 855-45(3) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

nodes.label: Reset the first element of cost base / reduced cost base to market value at the residence change time
nodes.body: On becoming an Australian resident, the first element of the cost base and reduced cost base of each qualifying CGT asset becomes its market value at that time (s 855-45(2)). Also, Parts 3-1 and 3-3 apply to the asset as if it were acquired at the time the individual/company became an Australian resident (s 855-45(3)). Note the effect is subject to s 768-950 (temporary residents).

nodes.label: Is the entity a trust that becomes a resident trust, or a CFC that becomes an Australian resident?
nodes.body: s 855-50 deals with trusts that become resident trusts (market value reset of trustee assets, mirroring s 855-45). s 855-55 deals with CFCs that become Australian residents — s 855-45 does NOT apply; instead the ITAA 1936 ss 411-414 modifications apply to the CFC's assets.

nodes.label: No reset — original cost base retained
nodes.body: Assets that are TAP or pre-CGT keep their existing cost base when you become an Australian resident. Gains accrued before residency remain potentially taxable if the asset is later disposed of as TAP.

nodes.label: Residency-change CGT position established — cost bases set for future CGT events
Is the asset an option/right to acquire TAP (item 4) or a s 104-165(3) disregarded asset (item 5)?
nodes.body: s 855-15 item 4: an option or right to acquire a CGT asset covered by item 1, 2 or 3 (TARP, indirect interest, PE business asset). Item 5: a CGT asset covered by s 104-165(3) — choosing to disregard a gain/loss on ceasing to be an Australian resident. If neither applies, the asset is not TAP.

nodes.label: Does the CGT event involve an underlying asset (D1, D2, F1 or J1)?
nodes.body: s 855-10(2): for CGT events D1 (creating contractual rights), D2 (granting options), F1 (granting a lease) and J1 (share becomes redeemable), the relevant CGT asset is the UNDERLYING asset — e.g. the land subject to an easement, option or lease, or the roll-over asset. Test TAP by reference to the underlying asset.
